The following section generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7, of the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. The Railroad, along with its subsidiaries and rail affiliates, is our one reportable operating segment. Although we provide and analyze revenues by commodity group, we treat the financial results of the Railroad as one segment due to the integrated nature of our rail network. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 2025 Results • Safety – Building on the foundation and commitment to our safety culture, 2025 furthered our progress towards world-class safety. With a focus on four central pillars – Injury Prevention, Leverage Technology, Situational Awareness Testing, and Peer-to-Peer Engagement, we are cultivating a safety-focused mindset so all of our employees return home safely each day. Injury Prevention efforts focus on specific, critical tasks where any form of non-compliance can result in a serious injury. Training is vital to teach our employees how to safely execute those critical tasks in order to reduce the risk of injury or derailment. By Leveraging Technology, we seek to eliminate or automate activities with the most risk. Over 7,000 wayside detectors monitor freight cars and locomotives in real time, generating 72 million data points daily to proactively identify and mitigate risks. We are building safer trains with our proprietary Physics Train Builder technology, which allows us to evaluate train and route characteristics to enable proactive intervention by our Operating Practices Command Center to prevent derailments. We utilize our autonomous geometry car fleet to inspect 500,000 miles of track annually. This technology and the data it provides enable us to direct investments and resources in the right place, helping to significantly reduce track-caused derailments over the last 10 years. Situational Awareness Testing (a program we call COMMIT) is our program that observes, tests, and coaches our employees to promote understanding and compliance with our work rules. COMMIT goes beyond traditional classroom learning, with an emphasis on in-the-field training with employees actively running the railroad. 28 Table of Contents Peer-to-Peer Engagement drives employee ownership through engagement with our safety programs. Our culture embodies a personal commitment to do our jobs with a passion for safety so everyone goes home safe. Employees are encouraged to speak up if they see unsafe behaviors. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The following discussion addresses significant factors, events, and uncertainties that make an investment in our securities risky and provides important information for the understanding of our “forward-looking statements,” which are discussed immediately preceding Item 7A of this Form 10-K and elsewhere. The risk factors set forth in this Item 1A should be read in conjunction with the rest of the information included in this report, including Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, Item 7, and Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, Item 8. We urge you to consider carefully the factors described below and the risks that they present for our operations as well as the risks addressed in other reports and materials that we file with the SEC and the other information included or incorporated by reference in this Form 10-K. When the factors, events, and contingencies described below or elsewhere in this Form 10-K materialize, our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, or prospects can be materially adversely affected. In such case, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose part or all of your investment. The disclosures in this section reflect our beliefs and opinions as to factors that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past or their likelihood of occurring in the future. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also materially adversely affect our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, and prospects. Strategic and operational risks We must manage fluctuating demand for our services and network capacity – Significant reductions in demand for rail services with respect to one or more commodities or changes in consumer preferences that affect the businesses of our customers can lead to increased costs associated with resizing our operations, including higher unit operating costs and costs for the storage of locomotives, rail cars, and other equipment; workforce adjustments; and other related activities, which could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition, and liquidity. If there is significant demand for our services that exceeds the designed capacity of our network or shifts in traffic flow that are contrary to the designed capacity of our network, we can experience challenges, including congestion and reduced velocity, that could compromise the level of service we provide to our customers. This level of demand also can compound the impact of weather and weather-related events on our operations and velocity. credit_strengths.text: Union Pacific's operating margin is exceptionally high relative to the Industrials sector median, reflecting the efficiency of its single integrated rail network and pricing discipline. This superior profitability provides a substantial buffer to absorb volume declines or cost inflation without impairing cash generation.

Interest coverage is comfortably above the sector median, with operating income covering gross interest expense multiple times. This strong fixed-charge cushion supports the current intermediate financial risk profile and provides headroom against a moderate earnings downturn.

key_risks.text: The company must manage fluctuating demand for rail services and network capacity. Significant reductions in demand for one or more commodities, or shifts in traffic flow contrary to designed capacity, can lead to congestion, reduced velocity, higher unit operating costs, and costs for storing locomotives and rail cars, materially affecting results.

Debt maturities are heavily weighted to later years, with the bulk due after year five, but the current portion still requires refinancing. A material rise in interest rates at refinancing could increase interest expense, pressuring coverage, though the company retains ample liquidity and market access.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditures, leaving free cash flow that represents a moderate share of debt. This internally generated liquidity supports scheduled maturities and provides a cushion, though the ratio sits below the sector median, indicating less relative debt reduction capacity.

Net leverage is modest and sits below the sector median on a cash-netted basis, but the company's shareholder distributions absorb most free cash flow. This limits deleveraging and leaves leverage sensitive to EBITDA declines, with limited headroom before breaching the next threshold.

overall_credit_view.text: Union Pacific's credit profile is supported by a strong operating margin, solid interest coverage, and a diversified rail franchise. The intermediate financial risk profile reflects leverage and cash-flow metrics that are adequate but not exceptional, with net leverage below the sector median and coverage above it.

Analyst judgement: the company retains investment-grade characteristics, but shareholder returns consume most free cash flow, constraining deleveraging. A sustained demand shock or higher refinancing costs could pressure metrics toward the next threshold. The stable revenue trend and safe Altman Z-score mitigate near-term concerns.

credit_strengths.text: Union Pacific 的營運利潤率相對於工業板塊中位數異常高，反映其單一整合鐵路網絡的效率及定價紀律。此優越盈利能力提供重大緩衝，以吸收運量下降或成本通脹，而不損害現金產生。
利息覆蓋率舒適地高於板塊中位數，營運收入覆蓋總利息支出多倍。此強勁固定費用緩衝支持當前中等財務風險狀況，並提供空間應對溫和盈利下滑。

key_risks.text: 公司必須管理鐵路服務及網絡容量需求的波動。一種或多種商品需求大幅下降，或交通流量轉移與設計容量相反，可能導致擁堵、速度降低、單位營運成本上升，以及機車和鐵路車輛儲存成本，重大影響業績。
債務到期嚴重集中於後期年份，大部分於五年後到期，但當前部分仍需再融資。再融資時利率大幅上升可能增加利息支出，壓力覆蓋率，儘管公司保留充足流動性及市場准入。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運現金流舒適地覆蓋資本支出，留下自由現金流，佔債務中等份額。此內部產生流動性支持預定到期並提供緩衝，儘管比率低於板塊中位數，表明相對債務減少能力較低。
淨槓桿適度，並以現金淨額基準低於板塊中位數，但公司股東分派吸收大部分自由現金流。此限制去槓桿，並使槓桿對 EBITDA 下降敏感，在突破下一門檻前空間有限。

overall_credit_view.text: Union Pacific 的信用狀況受強勁營運利潤率、穩健利息覆蓋率及多元化鐵路特許經營權支持。中等財務風險狀況反映槓桿及現金流指標充足但不卓越，淨槓桿低於板塊中位數，覆蓋率高於其。
分析師判斷：公司保留投資級特徵，但股東回報消耗大部分自由現金流，限制去槓桿。持續需求衝擊或更高再融資成本可能壓力指標趨向下一門檻。穩定收入趨勢及安全 Altman Z-score 緩解近期擔憂。
